name: Tainted Tablet

angles.text: As a warlock, you receive your first call to Nartok, your trainer in Durotar. He urges you to master the Nether instead of fearing it.
As an orc, you know demonic pacts brought catastrophe to Draenor. Fel magic remains controversial, so Durotar's warlocks counsel both secrecy and boldness.
As a member of the Horde, you know Thrall's new people are wary of demonic corruption. Warlocks in places like the Den say they can command Nether powers safely and secure their people's future.

faq.answer: Tainted Tablet is a written summons for an aspiring practitioner in the Valley of Trials. It directs you to Nartok, your trainer inside the Den.
Nartok sent Tainted Tablet. He is an orc warlock trainer inside the Den in the Valley of Trials, and calls newly arrived practitioners to instruction.
Nartok lives inside the Den, a cavern in the Valley of Trials where darker arts and specialized training take place out of sight.

Nartok warns you to guard your powers because ordinary folk may lash out in fear at what they do not understand. Orcs also remember the deep harm demonic corruption caused in their past, so warlocks keep their arts guarded and tread carefully.
faq.q: Why does Nartok warn to guard your powers closely?

faq.answer: Nartok believes those who master Nether entities can forge their own path and shape their people's fate. Where conventional leaders falter, warlocks can seize power instead of being enslaved by it.
faq.q: What is Nartok's view on practicing fel magic?

faq.answer: A local in the Valley of Trials passes you the tablet. They admit unease with fel spellcasters, but know Nartok's summons must be delivered.
faq.q: Who gives you the Tainted Tablet?

sections.body: A stone message passes through uneasy camp caretakers to newly arrived practitioners in the Valley of Trials. Nartok, a warlock trainer who makes his home inside the Den, calls them to him. He invites you to leave ordinary tribal duties and study deeper, forbidden magic.
sections.title: A Dark Summons

sections.body: Nartok speaks plainly about the troubled history between orcs and the Nether. He says the strong should command these volatile powers instead of rejecting them from shame or fear. Where ordinary chieftains falter, he believes those who cunningly master Nether entities can rise to prominence. Yet fearful minds strike at what they cannot understand, so these powers must be guarded closely.
sections.title: Commanding the Nether

summary: In the Valley of Trials, Tainted Tablet calls new practitioners to Nartok inside the Den. He teaches warlocks to command the Nether and shape their own fate, though its powers must be kept guarded.
